subject: gov.legislate
name: ICT Authority
milestone: The ministry briefed the President on establishing the body while awaiting the passage of legislation
position_end: Being established as a state entity under the ICT ministry while legislation is awaited (2026-08)
note: A May 2026 account states the President signed the Authority's legal framework; an August 2026 account states the government is establishing it while awaiting legislation. The two have not been reconciled, and the division of competence with the National Communication Authority is unstated. Reconcile attempt 1, 2026-08-09: no bill, act, presidential order or gazette entry can be found. The MoJCA law collection's most recent instrument is the Labour Act 2017 and it omits the Cybercrime and Computer Misuse Act 2026 too; the Office of the President's decrees page publishes no documents; the TNLA bills register stops in August 2023. The registers are not current enough for their silence to settle anything. Reconcile attempt 2, 2026-08-10, closed unresolved: both accounts trace to one speaker, the ICT minister, who on 2026-05-21 said the law is out already and signed by the president and on 2026-08-05 was reported standing the body up while parliament legislation is awaited. No instrument is retrievable because South Sudan has no operating gazette: on 2026-01-12 the President ordered a committee to launch the Official Gazette and clear a publication backlog of every law and decree since 2011, and no maiden edition is on file; signed presidential documents are classed privileged executive communication barred from being photographed, scanned or shared online. The Assembly publishes no Hansard - nla.gov.ss 404s on /hansard, /hansards and /documents and its bills and order-of-the-day pages are procedural explainers, not registers. The qualified status is the resting state and the brief is closed.

Reconcile attempt 1, 2026-08-09: no construction record exists in any reachable published source — the NCA's publications page carries five documents and none concerns the data centre, its news feed carries nothing on the build or on the oversight committee's output, the ICT ministry publishes nothing after 2025-12-18, and MGI Communications has made no statement. Reconcile attempt 2, 2026-08-10, closed unresolved: the World Bank EARDIP project P176181, the only Bank digital operation covering South Sudan, carries no data-centre workstream in its ISR of 2026-06-30 and the Bank archive returns nothing on the facility, so it is not donor-financed and no procurement record exists where one normally would; mgi communications ag is a privately held Swiss company of about nine people in Zug and files no public accounts. That ISR does establish dated that guidelines on government data hosting including cloud adoption were still unpublished at 2026-06-16, unchanged from the 2022-11 baseline against an 2028-04 target. It is also not established that there is only one facility: the regulator in 2026-01 describes MGI in the present tense as managing critical data centre infrastructure, while the minister in 2026-04 describes a centre being built and halfway complete. The dated stand-off is the resting state and the brief is closed.

name: New-generation passport and EAC passport
milestone: Announced for August 2027; ten-year validity would require amending the passport act
position_end: Announced intention with no legislative timetable; ordinary validity remains five years, and the immigration directorate has a route rather than a date - a memorandum submitted to the Inspector-General of Police, then the Minister of Interior, then the Council of Ministers, and finally the National Legislative Assembly, because the five-year limit is written into the law (2026-07)
note: the immigration handover of 9 August 2026 was reported as having extended adult validity to ten years; no amending instrument is on file and the directorate’s own account puts the change before the Assembly

subject: dpi.id
name: Passport issuance
milestone: Stock and tenure figures given at the 2026-08-09 handover of the directorate
position_start: Severe shortage across every passport category; issuance interrupted
position_end: Issuance running; the outgoing director of immigration and civil registry put stock at about 32,000 passport booklets and 172,000 national identity cards at the 9 August 2026 handover, alongside 100 new mobile registration kits, a Nairobi memorandum toward an integrated civil registration system, and adult passport validity extended to ten years. His successor says over a million people apply each year and that delays run to a month
sources: 2026-08-10-south-sudan-immigration-digital-reform-handover|2026-08-12-south-sudan-immigration-chief-citizen-testimony|2026-07-26-south-sudan-37000-new-passport-booklets-arrive|2026-01-16 Juba - Passport, ID card issuance resumes
note: the stock and clearance claims are the outgoing officeholder's own, made at his own handover; the annual applicant figure and the month-long delay are the incoming officeholder's

subject: dpi.id
name: Personal identity card (Butaka Shakhsia)
milestone: Required for banking, land transactions and court processes; 380,000 held by the directorate
position_end: 380,000 cards held by the directorate; required for banking, land and court (2026-01)
sources: 2026-01-16 Juba - Passport, ID card issuance resumes

subject: dpi.id
name: School-based national identity registration
milestone: School-based registration launched, August 2026
position_end: School-based national identity registration launched, and the immigration directorate's head set out a digital reform programme with a memorandum on an integrated registry; mobile registration kits were deployed from April 2026 (2026-08)

subject: dpi.id
name: Unified national digital identity system
milestone: Announced: a digital national identity card for every citizen aged 18 and over
position_end: Announced as intent only; no law, budget, timetable, vendor or platform named (2026-07)
note: Announced against a base in which the World Bank puts close to 90% of the population without any government-recognised identification.

subject: dpi.pay
name: Bilateral support for financial technology
milestone: Support reported August 2026
position_end: A bilateral partner is supporting the development of digital payment systems, with the central bank governor named in the account
note: no instrument, envelope, workstream or timetable is stated, and the base holds no domestic payment system for it to attach to

subject: dpi.pay
name: Cash payment of tax at revenue offices
status: Discontinued, and cash collection now ordered enforced
milestone: Cash enforcement ordered 2026-08-29
position_start: Cash accepted at revenue offices and by revenue officers
position_end: the economic reform committee ordering banks to enforce cash tax payments, reversing the direction the cashless measure set
note: Framed by the authority as a transparency and liquidity response and stated as temporary, until further notice.

subject: dpi.pay
name: Cashless payment for passports and identity documents
milestone: Cash abolished for passport and identity payments after a supply crisis
position_end: Cash abolished; digital payment only (2026-01)
sources: 2026-01-19 South Sudan introduces digital payment system for passports after supply crisis

subject: dpi.pay
name: Mobile money as legal tender
milestone: Affirmed by the Bank of South Sudan under the 2017 Electronic Money Regulation
position_end: In force; no conduct supervision of the operator on record
note: The target of 30% adult usage by 2027 is the central bank's own; economists called the declaration premature in an economy over 90% cash-based.

subject: dpi.pay
name: Mobile money services (MTN MoMo, Digitel)
milestone: Operators pledged nationwide agent expansion with the central bank
position_end: In service; no agent, account or transaction figures published

subject: dpi.pay
name: National Instant Payment System (NIPS)
milestone: Roadmap development announced with AfricaNenda after a 2023 proof of concept
position_start: Roadmap announced, full rollout targeted for December 2025
position_end: No go-live documented; South Sudan absent from AfricaNenda's 2025 instant-payments census (2026-07)

subject: dpi.pay
name: Public argument on accountability in digital payments
milestone: Published 2026-08-27
position_end: a published argument that digital payments are needed but must be accompanied by the ability to trace public money

subject: dpi.pay
name: South Sudan Interbank Payment and Settlement System (SSIPS)
milestone: Launched with 13 banks; all licensed banks mandated by 31 January 2026
position_end: Live: real-time gross settlement and automated clearing on ISO 20022, 13 banks at launch (2025-10)
note: Wholesale settlement infrastructure, not a retail instant rail; the retail framing used at launch was promotional.

subject: dpi.registry
name: Address and postal code register
status: Not held, searched 2026-09-06 - the statutory duty exists and nothing has been built under it
milestone: Statutory duty since 2012
position_end: Not established. The National Communication Act 2012 requires the Authority to establish a national postal system for addresses and postal codes; no address register, postcode scheme or addressing project is recorded under it (2012)

subject: dpi.registry
name: Birth registration coverage
position_end: About 90% of births going unrecorded (2026-07)
sources: 2026-07-22-south-sudan-id4d-country-diagnostic-national-id-gap|2025-12-15 Strengthening Civil Registration and Ending Statelessness in South Sudan

subject: dpi.registry
name: Centralised civil registration and vital statistics system
milestone: Announced: health facilities to notify births, the directorate to be sole issuing authority, death registration compulsory
position_start: Civil Registry Rules and a costed CRVS plan adopted; a birth-registration pilot at Juba Teaching Hospital (2025-12)
position_end: Centralisation announced as intent; no law, budget, timetable, vendor or platform named (2026-07)
sources: 2026-07-28-civil-registry-digital-system-birth-death-marriage|2025-12-15 Strengthening Civil Registration and Ending Statelessness in South Sudan

subject: dpi.registry
name: Digital land register
milestone: One expert's advocacy for a central digital land database; no programme, instrument or system is held
position_end: Not held

subject: dpi.registry
name: General Electoral Register
milestone: Registration still pending as at 21 August 2026
position_start: A statutory instrument without an exercise behind it: the National Elections Act 2012 requires the Commission to prepare, revise, update, approve and maintain the register (2012-04)
position_end: The Commission announced 22 December 2026 as the election date with a nationwide registration exercise of about a month to follow, and after assessment missions across all ten states and the three administrative areas said in August 2026 that registration was expected to begin soon - still pending (2026-08)

subject: dpi.registry
name: Register of Companies
milestone: Constituted by the Companies Act 2012
position_start: Constituted by the Companies Act 2012, with a statutory register and an office of Registrar (2012-02)
position_end: Constituted by the Companies Act 2012, with a statutory register and an office of Registrar; no registration count, digital filing route or turnaround figure is published (2012-02)

subject: dpi.registry
name: Register of South Sudanese Nationals
milestone: More than 4,000 cards distributed across Greater Yei, July 2026
position_start: Established by the Nationality Act 2011, which requires the Directorate of Nationality, Passports and Immigration to maintain the register (2011-07)
position_end: Distribution of more than 4,000 processed national identity cards and passports began in Yei River County covering the four counties of Greater Yei, with European Union support (2026-07)
note: No national coverage figure is published.

subject: dpi.registry
name: Social protection beneficiary registry
milestone: 87,867 households registered and paid across 15 counties
position_start: A government-led management information system linked to biometric beneficiary registration, project-scoped rather than a standalone universal social registry (2024-08)
position_end: 87,867 households, 615,069 people, biometrically registered and paid across 15 counties (2025-09)
note: Scoped to one project's caseload; no universal social registry exists.

subject: dpi.registry
name: Taxpayer register and Tax Identification Number
milestone: Registration enforced by public notice, May 2026
position_start: Required by the Taxation Act 2009: a registration system giving each taxpayer a unique identifying number, with registration mandatory and a certificate issued (2009-08)
position_end: Presidential Order No. 35 of 2025, signed 3 December 2025 and endorsed for enforcement in March 2026, requires every government institution to collect and remit public revenue exclusively through the revenue authority's electronic collection system; the authority's domestic tax division gave taxpayers to 15 May 2026 to clear arrears and warned that unregistered businesses without an identification number are acting illegally (2026-05)

subject: dpi.mis
name: Biometric registration of public servants
milestone: Third phase launched for the organised forces, June 2026
position_end: US$15m programme in its third phase; data held on a Ministry of Finance server (2026-06)
note: World Bank backed, to purge ghost workers and duplicate names; siloed from any identity layer, and no data-protection authority governs it.

subject: dpi.mis
name: Court case management system
status: Not held, searched 2026-09-06 - the justice chain outside Juba is described as barely functioning
milestone: No system recorded in the sector's own assessment
position_end: Not established. The most substantive assessment of policing and justice-chain capacity by state and county describes case management, police staffing and infrastructure gaps outside Juba, recording for one state that Wau remains the only county with a functional formal justice system (2022)

subject: dpi.mis
name: DHIS2 national health management information system
milestone: Predictive malaria dashboard piloted inside the national instance, July 2026
position_start: Operating at national and sub-national levels since 2020, with integration of health-programme data into it in progress, overall health information system maturity scored at 40.5 per cent and only 22.4 per cent of health facilities holding comprehensive facility-wide electronic systems (2025-02)
position_end: An electronic logistics management system reached 105 of 145 health facilities with its dashboard integrated into the national instance, and a custom dashboard began piloting climate-informed predictive modelling and automated malaria outbreak alerts inside it (2026-07)

subject: dpi.mis
name: Education in Emergencies Management Information System
milestone: Launched on the DHIS2 platform with UNESCO and the HISP Centre, after training 35 master trainers
position_end: Launched; 12 County Education Departments across six states equipped with solar power, computers and connectivity (2026-08)
note: Built on the same DHIS2 instance the health ministry has run since 2018; funded by Education Cannot Wait.

subject: dpi.mis
name: Education Management Information System
milestone: Costed national action plan produced, 24 March 2026
position_start: Four parallel education data systems assessed against a common framework and found to diverge on coverage, frequency and accessibility, with harmonised indicators and stronger cross-system coordination called for (2025-09)
position_end: The landscape described as largely manual and fragmented across multiple systems with limited integration and limited interoperability, and a costed national action plan produced over three days covering capacity development, data quality, infrastructure and system integration, governance and decentralisation (2026-03)

subject: dpi.mis
name: Land records and land administration system
milestone: State-level digital land registration framework under development, July 2026
position_start: Land administration described in the government's own draft policy as weak and largely manual, records often handwritten and formal administration concentrated in a few urban centres, with a National Land Registry and Land Records System set as a policy objective (2023-04)
position_end: Central Equatoria State's information ministry, with the state housing and lands ministry and county authorities, is developing a unified digital land registration framework beginning with land records in Juba County; a European Union and migration agency programme running in Rubkona and Yei River counties from 1 January 2026 commits to advancing the digitalisation of land records (2026-07)

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Crawford Capital e-Government concession
milestone: Exclusive e-Government services contract signed 16 November 2019 without competitive tender
position_start: In force, exclusive across trade permits, visas, tax, customs and work permits
position_end: In force; the contractor sanctioned by the United States in May 2026 and a ministerial review order overruled within 24 hours (2026-06)
note: The UN Commission puts the eServices profit share at 75% to the contractor; the company says it takes a 2% platform service fee, which describes a separate e-Tax contract. The two accounts have not been reconciled.

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Electronic cargo tracking
milestone: Introduced by the revenue authority for inbound goods
position_end: In use, to curb diversion and smuggling (2026-05)

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Electronic visa portal
milestone: Revised fees published on the portal, applications online only with a stated 72-hour processing time
position_end: In service; US$50 for citizens of Kenya, Uganda, Rwanda and DR Congo and US$100 for Somali, Burundian and Nigerian citizens (2026-07)
note: Fees are denominated in USD by the issuing authority; the portal runs inside the Crawford Capital concession, so the charge is levied through a privately operated channel.

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Ensoft telecom revenue-assurance build-operate-transfer
milestone: Six-year agreement signed by the revenue authority and the NCA; the vendor takes 3.56%
position_end: Signed; the NCA hosts and oversees the system and it transfers to the state after six years (2025-10)
note: The vendor is Ensoft in one account and N-Soft in another; no source on file settles the name.

subject: dpi.govtech
name: NCA e-Services Platform
milestone: Launched, digitising licensing, payments and regulatory workflows
position_end: Launched (2026-02)

subject: digital.localgov
name: State or county digital service delivery
status: Not held, searched 2026-09-06 - the most recent capacity assessment finds the institutions themselves short of the basics
milestone: Capacity assessed across the ten states and three administrative areas, April 2021
position_end: Not established. The most comprehensive assessment of state and local government institutions covers organisational structures, staffing, infrastructure and working environment across all ten states and the three administrative areas, and finds gaps across them; no state or county digital service platform is recorded (2021-04)

subject: digital.rural
name: Data capture in rural schools
milestone: Costed action plan produced, March 2026
position_start: The annual education census collecting school-level data on tablets into a web repository, covering enrolment, teachers, facilities and the availability of ICT teachers at schools nationally (2023)
position_end: School-level reporting documented as still largely manual with inadequate infrastructure and connectivity especially in rural and hard-to-reach areas, and a costed national action plan produced in response; 84 computers, 33 motorbikes and one vehicle were handed to the education ministry in November 2025 to strengthen monitoring and supervision (2026-03)

subject: digital.rural
name: Digitalisation of police stations
milestone: Forensic laboratory equipment donated and fifteen officers trained, June 2026
position_start: Policing capacity assessed by state and county with case management, staffing and infrastructure gaps outside Juba, one state recording about 1,000 police officials in total (2022)
position_end: Digital forensic laboratory equipment donated with electronic fingerprint technology planned for a second phase, and fifteen officers trained and tasked with training others in the states; a separately funded surveillance project was approved with a first phase limited to Juba and a stated second phase to expand nationally (2026-06)
note: No county station is confirmed to hold any of it.

subject: digital.rural
name: Digitalisation of rural health facilities
milestone: First patient-level electronic register in operational use, April 2026
position_end: The country's first patient-level electronic treatment register moved into operational use across five facilities including state hospitals at Rumbek, Yirol and Yambio, with more than 12,700 legacy records digitised and missed appointments falling from 58 per cent to 11 per cent between May 2025 and February 2026; an offline-first tracker on Android devices ran a twelve-month pilot for community health workers in remote settings, replacing paper household visit and immunisation follow-up reporting (2026-04)

subject: digital.rural
name: Registry offices outside Juba
milestone: 2,500 cards registered across Greater Yei, April 2026
position_end: An immigration directorate delegation to Yei River County reported 2,500 national identity cards registered across the greater Yei region to date, while recording that the county's own immigration office still lacks adequate and well-known premises (2026-04)

subject: tech.ai
name: Algorithmic food security early warning
milestone: Monthly alerts running across 78 administrative areas
position_start: A monthly sub-national early warning system combining conflict, price, climate and exchange-rate data through calibrated transformations and a weighted generalised linear model to raise alerts and estimate populations at risk across the 78 second-level administrative areas (2026-07)
position_end: A monthly sub-national early warning system combining conflict, price, climate and exchange-rate data through calibrated transformations and a weighted generalised linear model to raise alerts and estimate populations at risk across the 78 second-level administrative areas (2026-07)

subject: tech.ai
name: Junub Academy e-learning platform
milestone: Launched June 2026
position_end: A national e-learning platform launched by the mobile operator with an education organisation and the general education and ICT ministries, zero-rated on that operator's network and carrying artificial-intelligence-supported educational content (2026-06)
note: A government-partnered public service, not an internal administration system.

subject: tech.ai
name: National artificial-intelligence strategy or programme
milestone: EAC Declaration on Artificial Intelligence adopted, April 2026
position_start: The ministry stating that the country is working on establishing its own roadmap for artificial intelligence, alongside other African states (2024)
position_end: No national strategy; the country adopted the East African Community Declaration on Artificial Intelligence as one of eight partner states, committing to a regional fund, shared infrastructure, harmonised curricula and integration of AI into development planning, and the regional strategy for 2026-2031 went to a validation workshop in Kampala on 4 and 5 May 2026 (2026-05)
note: The ministry's own position is that infrastructure, data centres and trained people come first; no national strategy text exists.

subject: tech.ai
name: National Cyber-Security Task Force
milestone: First operational meeting held 16 July 2026
position_end: Stood up under Presidential Directive No. 03/2026 as a multi-agency task force and steering committee to enforce the Cybercrimes and Computer Misuse Act 2026 ahead of the December 2026 elections, including against false and misleading information; the justice minister had in April 2026 publicly dismissed a circulating report as an artificial-intelligence fabrication and warned of prosecution (2026-07)

subject: tech.industry
name: Domestic capacity in digital production
status: Not held, searched 2026-09-06 - the country diagnostic finds no manufacturing base and a nascent software sector
milestone: Fibre backbone construction announced for December 2025
position_start: A nascent digital business sector - ride-sharing, information technology support firms, technology-enabled agribusiness - with no domestic hardware manufacturing base, severe skills and infrastructure gaps and no national fibre backbone (2022-06)
position_end: Construction of a 2,400 kilometre national fibre backbone reaching the Indian Ocean through Kenya was announced to begin in December 2025, the largest enabling investment on record for the sector (2025-10)

subject: tech.industry
name: eSIM service
milestone: Launched by MTN South Sudan
position_end: In service; no take-up figures published

subject: tech.industry
name: Sarafa payments application
milestone: Launched on the App Store, 30 March 2026
position_end: A Juba-headquartered financial technology company founded in 2024 launched a stablecoin-backed multi-currency payments application (2026-03)

subject: tech.innovate
name: Business incubation and startup financing
milestone: Four-year incubator launched at the University of Juba, 16 April 2026
position_end: A pitch competition in Juba on 26 September 2025 saw 24 entrepreneurs compete and seven share EUR 90,000 in grants; a European Union-funded four-year incubator launched on 16 April 2026 targeting business incubation, acceleration and finance for 350 small and medium enterprises across seven regions, 30 per cent women-led and more than half youth-led (2026-04)

subject: tech.innovate
name: UniPod, University of Juba
milestone: Launched 16 August 2023
position_start: The country's first high-technology innovation hub, a US$1.2 million facility with woodwork, agri-food technology, textiles, electronics and augmented and virtual reality laboratories, established under a November 2022 memorandum (2023-08)
position_end: The country's first high-technology innovation hub, a US$1.2 million facility with woodwork, agri-food technology, textiles, electronics and augmented and virtual reality laboratories, established under a November 2022 memorandum (2023-08)

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Digital literacy in the civil service
milestone: Three digital skills centres under renovation, August 2026
position_start: Digital literacy found low in stakeholder consultations but not statistically measured, with no national statistics or third-party surveys, and a competency framework and learning programmes for civil servants planned in response (2023-01)
position_end: Renovation began on three government facilities designated as digital skills centres in Central Equatoria under a five-year programme reaching more than 8,000 people including 3,000 civil servants, and four ministry staff completed a public-service digital expansion programme in Wuhan (2026-08)
note: No national measure of civil service digital literacy exists.

subject: capacity.literacy
name: Digital literacy in the general population
milestone: National assessment commissioned, bids closing 25 June 2026
position_end: A 2,135-household connectivity needs and usage assessment across four refugee-hosting locations between 15 January and 26 February 2026 found 72 per cent of respondents aware of the internet, 66 per cent of internet users unable to use it as much as they would like on grounds of cost, devices and literacy, and 41 per cent of women and 20 per cent of men unable to read and write; a government tender closing on 25 June 2026 commissions a National Digital Skills Assessment, confirming no completed national measure exists (2026-06)
note: The household assessment covers refugee and host-community sites only and is not nationally representative.

subject: capacity.training
name: Aweil ICT Hub
milestone: Opened in Northern Bahr el Ghazal State, reported 2026-08-31
position_end: Opened by the mobile operator as a digital-skills training, scholarship and innovation facility in Northern Bahr el Ghazal State
note: an operator announcement; no capacity, budget, term or intake figure is published

subject: capacity.training
name: Digital Innovation for Skills and Knowledge programme (Central Equatoria)
milestone: Costed at US$2,806,100 for three centres training more than 8,000 people
position_end: A costed plan; no financier, signed commitment or start date named (2026-07)
note: The implementing partner supplied the budget; the state minister put the intake at 5,000 residents and 3,000 civil servants.

subject: capacity.training
name: Educational Technical Cooperation Project (China)
milestone: US$22,336,740 committed for the second phase
position_end: Committed across two phases; no later implementation record held
note: US$7,084,827 for the first phase in 2016 and US$22,336,740 for the second in 2020; both year-precise and stated in USD by the financier.

subject: capacity.training
name: Mobile-money entrepreneur training programme
milestone: 1,225 entrepreneurs graduated, 2026-08-24
position_end: 1,225 graduates over a year, with business guidance and seed funding from the partner and digital financial-literacy training from the operator
note: the operator's own account; no seed-funding total and no measure of what the training changed

subject: capacity.training
name: National curriculum framework, secondary
milestone: Mentorship programme kicked off across three schools, April 2026
position_start: Information and communications technology placed among the optional secondary subjects alongside Kiswahili, French, Arabic, arts and physical education, with the framework noting that many schools lacked facilities and that the subject would run as a stand-alone catch-up programme where they were absent (2013)
position_end: A mentorship programme stakeholder meeting at Juba Day Secondary School co-created an implementation plan for a mentorship scheme across three selected secondary schools, run by a telecommunications union fellow with vendor support (2026-04)

subject: capacity.training
name: University qualifications in computing
milestone: First public university in Unity State opened with computing programmes, February 2026
position_start: Computer science and information technology named as faculties or specialisations at the University of Juba, which runs a four-year bachelor's degree through its own school, and at two private university colleges (2025-03)
position_end: Bentiu University of Petroleum opened as Unity State's first public university with a bachelor's degree in computer science and a diploma in information technology approved among its initial programmes, and five public universities were equipped with twenty desktop computers and a projector each to strengthen research capacity (2026-02)

subject: capacity.research
name: Public research programme in digital or data science
milestone: Two policy analyses of the 2026 cybercrime and data protection instruments published
position_start: A regional information and communications technology policy think tank's legal analysis of the 2021 Cybercrimes and Computer Misuse Provisional Order, recommending court-order requirements for data access, a data protection law, ratification of the African Union convention and deletion of the offensive-communication provision (2021-11)
position_end: A digital rights research organisation arguing for a genuinely independent and resourced data protection authority rather than a bill alone, citing Uganda and Kenya as models, and a South Sudanese civil-society chapter publishing a clause-level breakdown of the Cybercrimes and Computer Misuse Act 2026 (2026-02)
note: Every contribution on record is from outside government; no public research programme is held.

subject: include.access
name: Complaint and grievance redress channels
milestone: Procurement complaints committee operationalised, April 2026
position_start: The Public Grievances Chamber established as the statutory citizen complaints mechanism against government institutions (2011)
position_end: The procurement authority operationalised its Complaints Review Committee as an independent administrative review route under the 2018 Procurement Act; three community peace desks were activated in Unity State to receive concerns and housing, land and property issues, against an information-ecosystem assessment finding 35 per cent of respondents needing guidance on how to submit a complaint and 42 per cent withholding feedback for fear of reprisal (2026-04)
note: No digital feedback channel is held; every route on record is in person or on paper.

subject: include.access
name: Disability inclusion
milestone: Disability-inclusive food security training package launched, July 2026
position_start: The National Disability Action Plan implementing the 2015 policy, setting interventions across data management, health care, rehabilitation, education and law (2020)
position_end: A teacher training programme funded through the education emergency fund trained 1,400 teachers in sign language, Braille and inclusive pedagogy across three national teacher-training institutes, and a disability-inclusive food security training package was launched in Wau and Juba in July 2026 (2026-08)
note: No accessibility requirement attaches to any government digital service on record.

subject: include.access
name: Gender equity commitments
milestone: Two projects launched in the period
position_start: A National Gender Policy in force, a 35 per cent quota for women in government under the revitalised peace agreement, and the anti-gender-based-violence and family law bills both still bills two years after introduction (2024-07)
position_end: Two peacebuilding fund initiatives launched with the government in July 2026 reaching more than 8,000 women and young people, 2,100 of them women and girls, with leadership, livelihoods, digital empowerment and community dialogue; and a regional project launched in Torit in August 2026 linking women's economic empowerment to land rights and governance (2026-08)
note: No sex-disaggregated figure for phone ownership, internet use or identity registration is published.

subject: include.access
name: Internet subscription tariffs
milestone: About 15 per cent increase reported
position_end: A published account reports internet subscription tariffs rising by approximately 15 per cent, across both mobile operators, at a time the writer describes the economy as already struggling
note: an opinion column is the whole of the evidence: no tariff schedule, effective date, regulator approval or operator statement is held, so the figure is a user's own comparison of two renewals

subject: include.access
name: Internet users and penetration
position_end: 1.9 million users, 15.7% penetration (2025)
note: Regulator's own figures; no later national measurement is held.

subject: include.access
name: Mobile data price
position_end: Raised twice by exchange-rate adjustment with no revised rate published (2026-07)
note: MTN cut tariffs 25% in December 2025, before the two adjustments.

subject: include.access
name: Operator tariff reduction
milestone: MTN cut tariffs by 25%, with the ICT ministry pressing for more
position_end: A 25% cut applied, subsequently overtaken by two exchange-rate adjustments (2026-07)

subject: data.statistics
name: National Strategy for the Development of Statistics
milestone: Agricultural statistics plan founded, May 2026
position_start: The first strategy, running 2014 to 2020, setting legal and institutional, human resource, statistical infrastructure and data development objectives on a US$58 million budget (2014)
position_end: The finance minister publicly committed government support to the statistics bureau in January 2026 covering the second strategy, legal reform, sustainable financing and administrative data; a five-day diagnostic workshop in May 2026 produced the foundation for a Strategic Plan for Agricultural and Rural Statistics for 2026 to 2031, aligned to that second strategy (2026-05)
note: The second strategy's own text is not held.

subject: data.statistics
name: Published national population estimate
position_end: About 16.36 million projected to end-2026 and 19.99 million to 2030 (2026-07)
note: Published by the National Bureau of Statistics at a World Population Day dialogue; about 2.2 million of the increase is attributed to migration from the Sudan conflict.

subject: data.statistics
name: Statistics from administrative data
milestone: 2025 annual health report published, February 2026
position_start: A flagship statistical abstract built on administrative health data covering health status, risk factors, service coverage and health systems across about ninety tables (2025-01)
position_end: The 2025 annual report of the health agency, organised by quarter and cluster, covers strengthened health information systems and administrative-data reporting alongside emergency response and primary health care (2026-02)
note: Health is the only sector publishing a statistical product from administrative data.

subject: data.open
name: Open government data portal or policy
milestone: Open data portal operating at the statistics bureau
position_end: The National Bureau of Statistics runs an open data portal with publicly accessible datasets, visualisation, multi-format download and interface access on public, registered and restricted tiers; the 2025 Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey was released publicly in April 2026 as the first nationally representative household dataset since independence, and the food security information system publishes a public dashboard of state-level phase populations (2026-05)
note: Scoped to statistical data; no whole-of-government open data policy or licence regime is held.

subject: data.satellite
name: Earth-observation or geospatial data programme
milestone: Satellite-derived indicators carried through the 2026 food security outlook
position_start: Crop monitoring triangulating field task force assessments and county crop monitoring committees with FAO and WFP satellite-derived vegetation index and rainfall data (2026-03)
position_end: Satellite-derived flood extent mapping used alongside rainfall and crop condition data to project Emergency outcomes across 34 counties and a credible risk of Famine in four through September 2026, and a monthly monitor combining vegetation index and rainfall with conflict, price and exchange-rate data to raise alerts across the 78 second-level administrative areas (2026-04)
note: Every product on record is produced by an external agency; no national earth-observation or geospatial programme is held.

subject: data.satellite
name: Meteorological observation network
milestone: Investment funding approved, February 2026
position_start: Three manual observation stations covering a country larger than Kenya, with forecasters newly trained to use satellite data and global numerical weather prediction outputs (2025-07)
